Module 1

The five-minute pitch

The pitch sells one idea: this real data center is half built, and its next part waits for the people in the room. Cast: the project lead, one student at the demo laptop, and the Dean for 40 seconds.

01
Lesson 1 · Module 1

Before the doors open

02
Lesson 2 · Module 1

Script

0:00–0:40The hookLift the rack by its handles.

"Quick question. What do you think this is? A speaker? A lunchbox? (Take two answers.) It's a data center. A real one. Right now it runs a firewall guarding its own network. The frame, the bays, even these handles came off a 3D printer. The machines inside are old or refurbished, given a second life. We call it Cyber-Soho."

0:40–1:20Why it matters

"Every place you will work, a hospital, a bank, a game studio, runs on machines like these. Every one of them is a target. You can read about that in a textbook. Here you learn it with your hands: you plug the cables, you write the firewall rules, you break it, and then you fix it."

1:20–2:20Live demoThe student sits at the laptop; the screen shows the IDS page.

"[Student] will play the attacker and scan our network, the first move a real attacker makes. (The scan runs.) Watch the screen. (The alert appears.) There. The firewall saw it in seconds and logged who, what and when. That's the job, and in this lab you're the one who writes the rule that catches it."

Fallback no alert within 15 seconds → "Live demos have a sense of humour. Here's the one we recorded this morning." Play the clip.
2:20–3:15Real industry platformsSwitch the screen to the platforms slide, or open Red Hat Academy live.

"And it's not only this rack. You log into the same platforms the industry trains on. Red Hat Academy builds you a classroom of live Red Hat Enterprise Linux servers. EC-Council iLabs give you real Windows machines to hack and investigate, with the full Academia library behind them: CEH, CHFI, CND and more. SAS teaches analytics and AI. Cisco, the networking provider the world runs on, gives you its full Networking Academy: Linux, cybersecurity, ethical hacking, even the Cyber Games America competition. You click Launch, and your lab is ready in about 20 seconds."

3:15–3:50What you will buildPoint at the empty bays.

"This is version one, and here's the plan. This term, four drives slide into these bays: a storage server that survives a dead disk. In January, two refurbished computers with 64 gigabytes of memory each turn this box into a private cloud. Then our own Git server, coding tools, and an AI model that runs right here, not in someone else's cloud. That AI node is the project waiting for you."

3:50–4:25The Dean

  • Why the department backs hands-on labs, in two sentences.

  • If funding is approved by then: announce it, then plug the DMZ cable into the firewall's DMZ port so the link comes up on screen.

  • If not yet: name what students will build this year.

4:25–5:00The askHold up a "Reserved" bay tag.

"So here's my question for you: who wants the next bay? Scan the code. Come up after and pick it up; it has handles for a reason. The lab is open. The next bay is empty. Come fill it."

Lesson 3 · Module 1

What students get from day one

These are screens from the platforms shown in the April 22 session; use them on the big screen or in comms.

Platform What students do there
Red Hat Academy Live RHEL 10 classrooms of six virtual machines, built on demand, with web or VNC consoles
EC-Council iLabs (Skillable) Launch hands-on labs such as System Hacking on Windows 11 VMs, ready in about 20 seconds
EC-Council Academia library eBooks and lesson plans for CEH, CHFI, CND, CPENT, CTIA, ECIH and the AI security certifications
EC-Council Learning Video courses such as Computer Hacking Forensics Investigator (CHFI) v11
SAS Training Course catalog in analytics, machine learning and AI with SAS Viya
Cisco Networking Academy Instructor-led classes in Linux Essentials, Introduction to Cybersecurity and Ethical Hacker; Python Essentials, IT Essentials certificates and the Cyber Games America 2026 competition track
CodeLab (Turingscraft) Python exercises mapped to popular textbooks

Each screen comes with a line to say while it is up. The lines follow how the platforms were presented in the April session, cut to 10–15 seconds each. Blur or crop personal names before any screen goes into public posts.

Lesson 4 · Module 1

Red Hat

Say

"This is IBM's Red Hat, the platform the industry uses to prepare for the most recognised Linux certifications. Every student gets a whole classroom of servers, live, online."

Say

"No install, no setup. You open a browser and you are root on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10. Learn it for the knowledge, or go all the way to the exam."

05
Lesson 5 · Module 1

EC-Council

Say

"If you want to be a cybersecurity expert, this is EC-Council, the people behind Certified Ethical Hacker. This is one of their labs: System Hacking."

Say

"Watch: one click, and they build you the whole lab while I talk. About 20 seconds."

Say

"Real virtual machines on the left, step-by-step instructions on the right. You practise the attack legally, then you learn to stop it."

Say

"And behind the labs, the full library: ethical hacking, forensics, incident handling, threat intelligence. The same books the certification candidates study."

Say

"Want to be the person who investigates after the breach? Computer Hacking Forensics Investigator is in there too."

Lesson 6 · Module 1

Cisco Networking Academy

Say

"Cisco is the networking provider the world runs on, and we have its courses at our disposal. These are live classes right now: Linux, cybersecurity, ethical hacking. Your professors are trained to teach them."

Say

"Courses lead to Cisco certificates you can show an employer, like this IT Essentials one. Linux, Python and cybersecurity sit right beside it."

Say

"And it's not only courses. This is Cyber Games America 2026, a cybersecurity competition track. Module one: threats, vulnerabilities and attacks. The same things our firewall just caught."

08
Lesson 8 · Module 1

Likely questions

Question Short answer
Do I need experience? No. The first labs start with plugging cables and reading logs.
Is hacking legal here? Only inside this isolated lab, on our own systems, under written rules.
What jobs does this lead to? SOC analyst, network or systems administrator, cloud and DevOps engineer.
Why not just use the cloud? We use it too. Building your own shows you what the cloud hides.
Which certifications can I prepare for? The platforms cover Red Hat, EC-Council (CEH, CHFI and more), SAS and Cisco tracks; ask which ones your programme includes.
How do I get involved? Through lab projects in your courses, and paid student-assistant hours when they open.

Pointers for Marketing & Communications

One message carries every post: our students build and defend a real data center that fits on a desk.

09
Lesson 9 · Module 1

Proof points

  • Built from a 3D-printed chassis and reused hardware; refurbished business computers join in January.

  • Runs free, open-source server software, the same tools companies use in production.

  • Students also train on Red Hat Academy, EC-Council iLabs and Academia, SAS, Cisco Networking Academy and CodeLab.

  • Students build it as graded lab work, and as paid assistants once funding is approved.

  • Power draw will be measured with a meter and published in watts, not guessed.

13
Lesson 13 · Module 1

Guardrails

  • Never show passwords, campus IP plans or dashboards with real data; the lab's demo dashboards with simulated traffic are fine.

  • Caption every attack clip "Simulated attack inside an isolated lab" / "Ataque simulado en un laboratorio aislado".

  • Say "running" only for what runs that day; everything else is "coming".

  • Written image consent from everyone filmed; visitors under 18 follow the University's policy for minors.

  • Credit line: "Cyber-Soho is a Cyber.SoHo Educational Hub design." Brand line: "From the Industry to the Classroom."

  • Hashtags: #CyberSoho #Ciberseguridad #Cybersecurity #MiniRack #Impresión3D #STEM
